newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound vs dollar, awaits fresh leads.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound vs dollar, awaits fresh leads.

text.p: * Ringgit seen in narrow range trading due to lack of fresh leads
* Tight dollar/majors movements also limiting activity
* Market awaiting release of Malaysia's trade figures, U.S. employment data
The ringgit was rangebound against the dollar in early Asian trading, and dealers said they expected a similar trend through the day.
"There's nothing to move the market. The ringgit only moved about 10 points in both London and New York overnight," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said local corporate selling and fears of central bank intervention would continue to cap the dollar's upside at 2.5190/5200 while offshore demand would limit its fall to 2.5140.
Tight trading in the dollar/majors also limited interest in the dollar/ringgit, they said.
Dealers said the market was waiting for the release of Malaysia's April trade data after speculation that it would be in deficit of up to two billion ringgit.
A Reuters poll of nine economists produced an average forecast of a 273.6 million ringgit deficit in April. Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
Dealers said market players were also awaiting the release of U.S. employment data later on Friday.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5150/60 a dollar against 2.5160/70 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
